scoring_rule: As B1 (and S3/S4/R2): a case is CORRECT iff every scored check holds and no exception is raised; check types claim, line, identical, custody (S3 run_checks) plus witness_binding (the G-INV witness's BIND_* list) and custody_why_contains. A SOUND case is correct when accepted; a BROKEN case is correct when rejected -- an accepted broken case is a survivor. Every case runs on two bases: 'synthetic' (fixtures.evidence_cases synthetic G0) and 'r1' (the committed C-009 fresh produce rso/binding/R1/G0, real executions, producer-bound). On the synthetic base the claim-type checks are recorded unscored (B1 finding: G-RECOMP fails on the fixture traces for every CL-RET claim, baseline included); the line, witness_binding, identical and custody checks there are scored. The r1 base is fully scored.

bundles.BASELINE: evidence_cases.g0(base) under the frozen code (fixture store: stage rows only; custody UNQUALIFIED by KEEPER_ROW_MISSING on both bases)
bundles.KEEPER: evidence_cases.keeper(base): registered manifest, inventory, table and stage records; custody QUALIFIED. Control only in this set (no keeper case)

gates: G-INV (BX5b: a FAILED re-execution of a presented node, after the cited row, with a digest, is provenance; BX4: no order read)
G-INV (BX5b: a second COMPLETED execution of a required node under the anchored launch, not presented; here parented to the presented execution's row, depth 2)
cases.note: The checks state what a qualifying consumer should do. binding.own_launch_rows reads parent_run_id == the launch (BX2's definition of a node execution row), so the reviewer predicts the frozen code ADMITS this shape; if the checks fail the case is an ADMITTED survivor for adjudication (CONTRACT s7 'under the anchored launch': transitive, or parent == launch?), not a scoring error.
